newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus pilot jailed for 1988 French crash.
newsitem.headline: Airbus pilot jailed for 1988 French crash.

text.p: A French court on Friday sentenced the pilot of an Airbus airliner which crashed during an air show in 1988, killing three people, to six months in jail for manslaughter with another 12 months suspended.
The Air France Airbus A320 had ploughed into a forest after a very low altitude pass over an airfield at Habsheim, near the eastern city of Mulhouse, killing three of the 130 passengers.

At the trial, pilot Michel Asseline blamed the aircraft's computer displays and alleged the flight recorders had been tampered with. But the prosecution said he and co-pilot Pierre Mazieres had recklessly endangered the passengers' lives.
Mazieres was given a one-year suspended sentence.

Three other officials, including Air France's director of flight operations at the time, Air France's then security director and the organiser of the air show at which the accident occurred, received suspended prison terms of six months or less.
The prosecution said Air France had regularly run low-altitude demonstration flights with passengers aboard in violation of civil aviation safety regulations.
